'''René Turlay''' (1932–2002) was a French [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]].

==Biography==
René Turlay was one of the four discoverers of charge-parity violation.

In 1957, he joined the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives|CEA]] laboratory. His first work with the Saturne [[synchrotron]] concerned the study of pi meson production in nucleon-nucleon collisions at 2.3 GeV. After his doctoral thesis, he went to [[Princeton University|Princeton]] as a post-doc.

From 1962 to 1964, René Turlay played a major role in all phases of the memorable experiment at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory|Brookhaven]]'s accelerator where the [[CP violation]] phenomenon in weak interactions was discovered. This work won the 1980 Nobel Prize.

From the 1970s and until after he retired, Turlay worked regurlary at the [[CERN|European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN)]] in [[Geneva]] on a number of different projects.<ref name="cernCour">{{cite web|url=http://lib-docs.web.cern.ch/lib-docs/Archives/biographies/Turlay_R-200302.pdf/|title=René Turlay 1932-2002|publisher=[[CERN]] Courier|first=Bernard|last=Peyaud|date=January–February 2003|accessdate=2019-07-15}}</ref>
